text: TWO MORE PROMOTIONS from applying the corrected ranking principle to already-scoped slices. (1) CREDENCE (core/ids.scala:142) is now FIRST in slice 2. Its Scaladoc invariant - 'a calibrated value is present only if the calibration model that produced it is named' - IS design-contract rule 3, one of the thirteen non-negotiables. fromProduct mints a calibrated probability with no named model in one line. Nine modules carry it: amr-interop, codec, core, features, fixtures, interview, laws, proposition, story. (2) COVERAGE (features/estimate.scala:102) is promoted within slice 3. Its doc: 'every aggregate must say how much of its support it actually observed'; construction validates observed <= eligible and both nonnegative. EIGHT modules carry it and it is THE support carrier ADR 0003 leans on, so forging one makes the support claim of any estimate it is attached to false. Coverage.+ constructs directly without revalidating - safe for two valid operands, but a forged Coverage PROPAGATES through every aggregate it touches. NOTE features/estimate.scala is reserved to the scout for MissingReason.Custom; this is ranking, not scheduling. THE PATTERN, now confirmed four times: the worst types to leave forgeable are those whose DOCUMENTATION MAKES A PROMISE - AuthorizedRemoteRequest (no code path hands raw text to a provider), CheckedSidecarPrelude (verified against evidence outside the file), Credence (calibrated implies named model), Coverage (an aggregate says how much support it observed). All four promises are currently false, and none was ranked highly by the original self-validation heuristic - three have no self-validating companion at all. Slice takers: if a type's Scaladoc makes a promise and it is ranked low, move it up and tell the chief.
